answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: every agent escrows tokens to join, and the deposit is slashed when peers detect colluding duplicates. A sybil attacker must pay that bond once per fake account, so fielding a thousand impostors costs a thousand deposits rather than nothing. Honest agents recover the bond through real service, but a duplicate farm only loses it, making impersonation unprofitable. Picture the network at its zenith: an umber audit trail shows stake flowing like a river from each escrow, revealing accounts that draw from one source and never earn independently.
